pilot.question: Can a small LoRA adapter improve bilingual identifier preservation, bounded source support and warranted abstention over the same unadapted trainable model, without increasing critical factual errors?
pilot.not_claimed: General architectural truth or independent verification; 16 updates cannot establish broad documentation competence.
pilot.model_selection: Owner-approved compatible trainable base/tokenizer pinned by revision/hash, preferably corresponding to existing deployment. Quantization/conversion and tokenizer differences are explicit confounds. No model selection/download authorized here.
pilot.dataset: Only separately owner-approved original synthetic or clearly licensed public training targets, grouped by source family/lineage and bilingual task. Exclude all current six public evaluation families, related dependencies, private Viva Bem and unapproved original 305 records. Minimum pilot review batch proposed: four bilingual task pairs; never assume approval.
pilot.baseline: Freeze unadapted trainable base inference with identical tokenizer/template/prompt/source cut/sampling/token limits and hardware; compare adapter under same conditions. Existing production GGUF is a separate deployment baseline. Preserve deterministic source-first rendering as a non-neural reference, not a trained-model improvement.

proposed_limits.lora_modules: Explicit approved exact module names after inspecting chosen base; never accept omitted/global defaults.
proposed_limits.scale: Must be verified against pinned framework semantics; no assumed alpha/rank convention.

pilot.preflight: Verify true tokenizer/template output and shifted loss mask; no supervised target may be lost to truncation, and padded targets must be excluded. Validate actual module counts/dtypes/shape/working-set feasibility before authorizing any update. Memory threshold and OS pressure response require owner-approved host-specific budget.
pilot.evaluation: Freeze unseen source-family tasks and deliberately incorrect claims before launch. Score complete bilingual outputs, per-claim support, unsupported claims, critical errors, exact identifiers, parity and justified abstention with separate verifier. Report paired counts, not just percentages; do not use training examples as independent evaluation.
pilot.success_gate: On the same frozen evaluation set: higher complete-output acceptance than unadapted baseline; no increase in critical factual errors or false verifier acceptance; identifier and language coverage nondecreasing. At least one complete output must pass all frozen dimensions. Tiny pilot results are feasibility evidence, not general accuracy.
stop_conditions: Memory-pressure threshold or wall budget exceeded
Checkpoint unable to preserve required state
pilot.preservation: Pin base/tokenizer/framework/data/code/prompt hashes. Save adapters, metrics and raw outputs; preserve optimizer/RNG/data position if exact resume is claimed. If only weights were saved, label a later run as a new weights-initialized experiment, never exact resume. Keep original GGUF and all old artifacts untouched.
pilot.rollback: A pilot adapter must not replace production. Restore original manifest/model/digest and demonstrate adapter disabled before any separately approved deployment. No fusion, upload, production switch or remote persistence is authorized.
owner_decisions: Approve model/tokenizer/framework and separate installation/download scope
Approve independent evaluation protocol and host resource budget
Authorize a specific future training run only after gates pass

note: Proposed constants are not executable configuration or automatic approval.
